answer.decision: Use logical replication with a brief write pause, validation, and traffic switch.
answer.action: Keep the source authoritative while continuously replicating to the target. Before the approved window, verify replication health, rollback readiness, monitoring, and explicit abort thresholds. During cutover, pause writes, drain in-flight transactions, wait for replication lag to reach zero, compare row counts and checksums, then switch traffic. Resume writes only after checks pass; if they fail or the window approaches its limit, route traffic back to the still-authoritative source.
reasons: The strategy can fit the sub-10-minute write-unavailability limit because peak staging lag was 42 seconds and validation tooling is available.
Keeping the source authoritative until validation completes preserves a tested rollback path and minimizes the chance of silently losing committed writes.
The 30-minute big-bang freeze violates the approved 10-minute cap, while full export/import is far too slow at 96 minutes.
Dual-write is disproportionately risky because the application has 19 write paths across six modules, including three paths that bypass the main repository layer.
Logical replication is the only option already rehearsed in staging and does not require coordinating a two-week application-wide write-path change with a four-engineer team.
assumptions: Production logical replication behavior is sufficiently similar to the peak-load staging rehearsal to complete catch-up and validation within the maintenance window.
Writes can be reliably paused and in-flight transactions drained before the final replication catch-up.
The target remains read-only until the switch, and no target-only writes occur before correctness checks complete.
Rollback within the validation phase means returning traffic to the source before target writes are accepted; later reverse replication is outside the cited rollback drill.
risks: Production replication lag or checksum validation may exceed rehearsal results and force an aborted cutover.
Schema, sequence, large-object, trigger, or replication-filter differences may not be detected by row-count checks alone.
A write-pause mechanism that misses a bypass path could permit late source writes or cause inconsistent switching.
Once writes resume on the target, rollback becomes materially harder unless reverse replication or another reconciliation procedure has been prepared and tested.
With no overnight vendor support, an unexpected database-specific failure could prolong recovery despite the four-engineer team.

citations.claim: Peak synthetic-load staging rehearsal showed 42 seconds of logical-replication lag.
Dual-write would need to cover 19 write paths across six modules, including three repository bypasses.
Rollback to the source was drilled in 7 minutes while the source remained authoritative.
Full export/import took 96 minutes in rehearsal.
The approved maintenance window caps write unavailability at 10 minutes.
CDC monitoring can compare row counts and checksums during cutover.
